title: Build an evidence-grounded document assistant
summary: Find the right passage, cite it, and make missing answers visible.
outcome: A document assistant with traceable sources and a retrieval evaluation set.
prerequisites: Work with Python lists and dictionaries.
Complete the testing refresher; structured-output practice is useful but optional.
teaching_question: Which answer failures begin with retrieving the wrong passage?

lessons.title: Prepare documents with stable citations
lessons.objective: Keep each passage connected to its original document.
lessons.explanation: Use a few documents you own. Split on paragraph boundaries first and preserve offsets and document identifiers. Very small chunks can lose context; very large chunks can bury the answer. Inspect a boundary example before choosing a more complex splitter.
lessons.example:
text = "Refunds take five days.\n\nContact support for damaged items."
chunks = []
start = 0
for part in text.split("\n\n"):
    chunks.append({"text": part, "start": start, "end": start + len(part)})
    start += len(part) + 2
assert all(text[c["start"]:c["end"]] == c["text"] for c in chunks)
lessons.exercise: Prepare five short documents and preserve each chunk’s document ID and offsets. Include an answer that spans two paragraphs and inspect whether your split loses necessary context.
lessons.completion_check: Every chunk resolves to exact original text, and the boundary case has a documented treatment.
lessons.artifact: A small document collection and citation-preserving chunker.

lessons.title: Measure a keyword baseline
lessons.objective: Return ranked passages before introducing embeddings.
lessons.explanation: A token-overlap baseline makes retrieval behavior inspectable. It often misses paraphrases and rewards irrelevant word overlap; those failures establish useful comparison cases. Choose a stable tie-break and return no result when every score is zero.
lessons.exercise: Write ten questions and their relevant document IDs. Return the top three passages using the baseline, then inspect one paraphrase failure. Embeddings are an optional follow-up experiment, not a prerequisite.
lessons.completion_check: You can reproduce which relevant passage was missed and calculate recall at three with an explicit denominator.

lessons.title: Cite answers and abstain on missing evidence
lessons.objective: Separate retrieved material from an instruction to the model.
lessons.explanation: Pass only selected passages to an answer adapter, keep their IDs and require an explicit missing-answer result. Citation existence is only a structural check: a human still needs to inspect whether the cited passage supports the answer. Retrieved text cannot authorize actions.
lessons.exercise: Use a fixed answer adapter first. Test an answerable question, an absent answer, an invented citation and a passage containing an instruction to ignore the user. Label model-backed results separately.
lessons.completion_check: Unknown citation IDs are rejected; absent answers remain explicit; source text never grants tool authority.
lessons.artifact: An answer contract with citation and abstention cases.

lessons.title: Find whether retrieval or answering failed
lessons.objective: Evaluate the two stages separately on frozen questions.
lessons.explanation: Label the relevant passages before judging generated answers. A missing passage is a retrieval failure; an unsupported answer despite a good passage is an answer failure. Include edited and deleted documents so citations cannot silently point to stale content.
lessons.exercise: Reserve eight questions for final evaluation. Compare retrieval and answer failures, make one development-set change, and report the held-out outcome plus a missing-answer case.
lessons.completion_check: The report distinguishes recall, supported answers and correct abstention, and states whether a real model ran.
lessons.artifact: A retrieval/answer failure matrix and reproducible checks.

editorial_status: Draft curriculum; maintainer and learner review pending
assumptions: 10–15 hours weekly is an editable estimate.
Start with standard-library fixtures. Optional libraries and a compatible model runtime need separate setup.
No paid service, model download or hardware capability is assumed.
